new_grants.title: Awesome Foundation Conservation and Climate Microgrant, November 2026
new_grants.funder: Awesome Foundation — Conservation and Climate Chapter
new_grants.eligibility: Individuals and small teams worldwide, including African applicants, with innovative nature-conservation or climate projects close to implementation. Applicants must be able to receive funds through PayPal, Wise or Venmo. Apply in English. Personal expenses, marketing, salaries, running costs, established projects, travel, political and religious projects are excluded. Previous grantees must wait 12 months.
new_grants.summary: A non-repayable microgrant for original conservation and climate ideas where US$1,000 can enable a practical project. Use the worldwide Conservation and Climate chapter rather than a geographically restricted local chapter.
new_grants.notes: The official worldwide chapter invites applications, lists November 27, 2026 as the next review deadline, and links a live chapter-specific form. No closing time or timezone is published. Later listed review deadlines are not extensions. The official FAQ confirms grants are not loans or investments.

new_grants.title: Pollock-Krasner Foundation Grants for Visual Artists
new_grants.amount: Up to US$50,000; most grants around US$35,000
new_grants.eligibility: Professional visual artists worldwide, including eligible African applicants, primarily working in painting, sculpture or works on paper/printmaking. Minimum 10 professional exhibitions in the past 10 years; active exhibition history and recent work required. Academic study, most students, primarily photography/video/performance/commercial art/craft and AI-generated work are excluded. Applicants from sanctioned countries must contact the funder before applying. Applications in English; reapplication waiting periods apply.
new_grants.summary: Unrestricted one-year support for professional visual artists. Apply online with a cover letter, statement, CV, 10 recent artwork images and three professional references. Review normally takes 9–12 months; this is not an emergency grant.
new_grants.notes: Official guidelines explicitly accept year-round applications and artists worldwide. The official-linked Blackbaud/YourCause programme route returned HTTP 200; real browser rendering reached the loaded Applicant Portal sign-in and Create account controls. No account or application was created.

new_grants.title: Front Line Defenders Protection Grants
new_grants.deadline: No application deadline published; the official secure form currently accepts protection-grant applications.
new_grants.amount: Up to €7,500; generally not 100% of the budget
new_grants.eligibility: Human rights defenders at risk and their organisations, including African applicants listed in the country selector. Support must address specific risks linked to peaceful human-rights work: physical/digital security, legal or medical costs, or certain family assistance. Not general project funding. Excludes international organisations, retrospective or duplicate funding, defenders already in exile, office running costs, vehicles, armed guards and general living costs. Reporting and receipts required.
new_grants.summary: Rapid practical support for the protection of human rights defenders facing threats because of their work. Use the official encrypted application form and specify safe contact details. Grant conditions require unused or ineligible funds to be returned.
new_grants.notes: The official programme explicitly invites secure applications and its live form states that users can submit a Protection Grant application online. Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana and other African countries are available in the official selector. No deadline is published; do not classify this as rolling merely from a missing deadline.

new_grants.title: Urgent Action Fund-Africa Protection Grants
new_grants.deadline: We provide grants throughout the year and have no funding cycle. You can submit your application as soon as an urgent situation requires it.
new_grants.amount: US$5,000 ceiling for Defending the Defenders grants, as listed in the official FAQ
new_grants.eligibility: Women-led, women-centric organisations or collectives based in Africa, with at least 70% women-identifying membership and women in decision-making roles. Informal groups may apply using a registered fiscal sponsor. Individual support must be through an organisation; no transfers to individual bank accounts. Interventions must be strategic, unanticipated, time-urgent, sustainable and supported, and address activists’ safety/security/wellbeing. Organisations outside Africa implementing African projects are ineligible.
new_grants.summary: Protection support for African women human-rights defenders and their organisations, movements or collectives. Apply using the official protection form; downloadable forms may also be sent to proposals@uaf-africa.org. Ordinary planned activities and routine running costs are not supported.
new_grants.notes: The official apply page links this live protection form; the official FAQ explicitly confirms year-round intake, Africa eligibility, sponsorship rules and the Defending the Defenders ceiling. This record is solely the Protection route. Rapid Response and Advocacy routes are excluded because their separate form ceilings conflict with the FAQ.
